decisions.decision: A malformed stored `due` stops the entire service at startup with an error identifying the ticket field, even with `DUE_TIMES` off.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the service to start with due times disabled and report the bad field for operators to repair before enabling them.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-6 behavior and malformed-time acceptance case (lines 29–30)

decisions.decision: The initial backfill uses each existing ticket's priority as it stands when the new service starts.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the priority recorded at creation so that later priority changes have no effect on the deadline assigned to an older ticket.

decisions.decision: The initial backfill uses the response hours configured at the time of backfill.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the stated 4, 24, 72 and 168 hour schedule applied to the pre-release backlog, with configured overrides applying only to new tickets.
decisions.where: record/01-intake.md, Q2 default (line 81); repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-2 and R-6 behavior (lines 13 and 29)

decisions.decision: Tickets opened while `DUE_TIMES` is off still have their deadlines set and saved at creation, using the hours in effect then.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted tickets opened during the disabled rollout period to receive their deadlines in a final backfill using the schedule approved for activation.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-1 acceptance boundary (line 10); record/04-spec.md, review summary (line 67)

decisions.decision: The audit history omits deadlines both when they are first assigned to new tickets and when existing tickets are backfilled.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the audit history to record the initial deadline assignment so staff can verify what response time was promised.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-4 behavior and acceptance (lines 21–22), and R-6 behavior (line 29)

decisions.decision: With `overdue=true`, a ticket must be overdue and match the existing status-or-priority filter when both of those filters are supplied.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted an overdue ticket to match both the requested status and priority, in line with the documented list semantics.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-5 behavior (line 25); repo/docs/shiploop/environment.md, Platform facts (line 15); repo/docs/api.md, List tickets (lines 76–77)

decisions.decision: An explicitly empty `DUE_HOURS_*` variable uses the built-in hours for that priority.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted a blank override to fail startup so operators discover a missing configuration value before deadlines are assigned.

decisions.decision: Existing requester notifications keep their current content when due times are on.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the ticket receipt to include the promised response deadline when due times are on.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-9 behavior (line 41); repo/docs/api.md, Create a ticket (lines 58–65)

decisions.decision: The overdue list uses the ordinary ticket-ID order and cursor pagination after applying the overdue filter.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted overdue tickets paginated by earliest due time so staff see the longest-overdue tickets first.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-5 behavior and acceptance (lines 25–26) and R-9 behavior (line 41); repo/docs/api.md, List tickets (lines 79–86)

decisions.decision: The `due` field is an ISO 8601 UTC string in the same format as `created`.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted a numeric Unix timestamp for clients that compare deadlines numerically.

decisions.decision: A PATCH body containing `due` is rejected with HTTP 400 as an unknown field.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted clients to be able to send back an unchanged `due` in a PATCH body while still rejecting attempts to change it.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-3 behavior (line 17); record/01-intake.md, Q7 default (line 126)

decisions.decision: A ticket enters the overdue list only once the current time is strictly later than its deadline.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted a ticket to count as overdue at the instant its deadline is reached.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-5 behavior and equality acceptance case (lines 25–26)

decisions.decision: The change is assigned release number 1.5.0 in the package and changelog.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted to choose the new version with the release team and make the bump in a separate release step.
decisions.where: record/01-intake.md, Q10 default (line 153); repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-10 behavior (line 45)

decisions.decision: The ordinary `npm test` run must exercise rollback with real 1.4.0 code even in a source checkout without Git history.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the real 1.4.0 compatibility check to run separately against the release artifact during release validation.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-8 acceptance (line 38); record/04-spec.md, review summary (line 67)
